The Client - Operations Coordinator, owns the client-facing coordination work inside STR Search's operations function. This role provides supplementary coordination support to the Client Success Lead and contributes to internal operations and team experience as capacity allows.

A note on AI: as a company, we're actively building in AI and automation solutions across the business. Some tasks this person handles today will eventually be automated. We're looking for a Channel & Partner Operations Partner to serve as the operational backbone of Procore's global partner business. In this role, you'll partner directly with the Vice President, Partners to turn partner strategy into the processes, data, and operating rhythm required to scale a reseller, distributor, and referral motion worldwide.

This is a build role. Procore's partner ecosystem is growing quickly, and much of the operating infrastructure - how we measure partner-sourced and partner-influenced business, how deals get registered and channel conflict gets resolved, how partner performance rolls into the broader revenue picture - is still being defined. You'll own that build. If you've done channel operations at scale and want the chance to design it rather than inherit it, this is that job.

This position reports to the Director, CCO Revenue Operations Business Partners and will be based remote in either Canada or the US. We're looking for someone to join us immediately.

What you'll do
• Serve as the primary operational business partner to the VP, Partners, translating global partner strategy into scalable processes, operating cadence, and measurement across reseller, distributor, and referral motions
• Build Procore's partner measurement foundation from the ground up - partnering with Revenue Insights to define partner-sourced and partner-influenced attribution logic, establish sanctioned data and source of truth, and stand up the reporting and dashboards partner leadership runs the business on
• Design and operationalize deal registration end to end: policy, workflow, SLAs, and the channel conflict resolution model between partner and direct motions, in partnership with Sales, Deal Desk, Legal, and Systems
• Establish the global partner operating rhythm, including pipeline and forecast reviews, partner performance reporting, and executive-level business reviews
• Partner with Revenue Planning on partner targets, quota, and capacity assumptions, bringing channel-specific productivity inputs and market context into the annual and in-year planning cycles
• Act as the business voice into Systems and IT on partner data architecture, PRM, and Salesforce requirements - defining what the business needs and validating that it works, in close partnership with the system owners
• Support the mechanics of two-tier distribution, including partner hierarchy, account and opportunity data integrity, and the operational handoffs across the partner lifecycle
• Complete qualitative and quantitative analysis to identify root cause deficiencies in the partner operating model, and track the effectiveness of improvements over time
• Build a strong internal network across NAMER, EMEA, and APAC to drive consistent adoption of partner processes globally while accommodating legitimate regional differences
• Support the development of partner policies and program documentation as the operating model matures

What we're looking for
• BA/BS degree is preferred; MBA or similar advanced degree is a plus
• 6+ years of revenue, sales, or business operations experience, including direct channel or partner operations experience supporting reseller, distributor, and/or referral motions
• Demonstrated experience building partner reporting and attribution from an early or undefined state - you've had to decide what "partner-sourced" means, defend it, and operationalize it
• Working knowledge of deal registration design and channel conflict management
• Experience supporting a global partner organization, with an understanding of how reseller and distributor motions differ across regions
• Experience at a large scale technology company is required
• Salesforce fluency; familiarity with PRM platforms and partner data models
• Adept problem solving and analytical skills; demonstrated ability to structure ambiguous problems, develop solutions, and craft high-quality executive presentations
• Strong communication skills with the ability to present to large groups and use storytelling to align multiple parts of the business
• Ability to collaborate and build effective relationships with Procorians at a range of levels and across different roles in the organization
• Comfort operating in white space with a high sense of urgency and the flexibility to pivot as the partner strategy evolves

Additional Information

Base Pay Range:
104,000.00 - 143,000.00 CAD Annual

This role may also be eligible for Equity Compensation and/or Bonus Incentive Compensation. Procore is committed to offering competitive, fair, and commensurate compensation. Actual compensation will be based on a candidate's job-related skills, experience, education or training, and location.

FFC is building the first integrated fusion fuel cycle, UNITY 2, at CNL’s Chalk River Laboratories. Commercializing that capability requires defined service offerings and strategic partnerships, a supply chain able to deliver first-of-a-kind (FOAK) engineered systems, and an operating model that scales with the business.
The Associate, Strategy & Business Operations supports three key pillars:

Commercial — build FFC’s service offerings and strategic partnerships from the ground up.

Business Operations — build the operating foundations of a scaling company and support executive priorities across the business.

Supply Chain — strengthen the supply chain strategy and supplier base for FOAK delivery and future commercialization.

Working across every FFC function, the executive team, and parent companies the scope of the role will broaden as the organization scales, with a path to greater ownership and responsibility.
Roles and Responsibilities:
Commercial — Service Offerings & Strategic Partnerships

This is design-and-build work and opportunity tracking and pipeline administration sit with Business Development.
• Strategy and analysis — define which markets, partners, and offerings FFC prioritizes and how to structure each, backed by market research and business cases.
• Offering design — build offerings from first principles, including scope, delivery model, resourcing, the split between FFC and its parent companies, and the cost, pricing, margin, and risk allocation behind each.
• Governance and implementation — design how partnerships and offerings are run (decision rights, approval gates, templates), then take them from paper into practice, including the agreements and partner-facing material behind them.
• Bids and proposals — coordinate inputs from FFC and parent company contributors, and draft assigned sections and pricing volumes.
Business Operations & Strategic Initiatives
• Operating model and tools — design and implement how FFC runs, including structures, decision rights, workflows, and the tools and tech stack behind them, and drive operational effectiveness.
• PMO and project delivery — build PMO capability, and support priority projects through planning, risk management, and progress reporting to leadership.
• Strategic initiatives and executive support — lead special projects for the executive team as priorities emerge, prepare executive and Board-level material, and support budgets and forecasts.
Supply Chain
• Sourcing strategy — contribute to the sourcing approach for FOAK and long-lead systems, and support make-versus-buy and key supplier decisions.
• Supplier base — build a qualified, performance-managed supplier base with Engineering and Quality, and design repeatable sourcing processes as FFC scales.
Must Have
• Bachelor’s degree in Business/Commerce/Economics, Engineering, or a related field; MBA or other advanced degree an asset.
• 3-5 years in management consulting, investment banking, private equity, transaction advisory, corporate development, or strategy and business operations roles; commercial or supply chain experience is also relevant.
• Track record of taking ambiguous problems from a blank page to a delivered outcome (a new offering, partnership, process, function, or client engagement), and comfortable with shifting priorities in an early-stage, scaling organization.
• Strong structured problem-solving: able to own analysis with limited direction, from raw data to a clear recommendation.
• Advanced Excel and financial modeling skills, including business cases, investment cases, and cost and pricing models.
• Excellent written and verbal communication, and the ability to produce client-, partner-, executive-, and Board-ready material in PowerPoint.
• Strong stakeholder management, able to influence senior leaders across technical and commercial teams and manage multiple workstreams to deadline.
• Comfortable using AI tools for research, drafting, and analysis, and interested in the systems and tools that help a business scale.
• Eligible to work in Canada, able to travel to Ottawa and other locations as required (aprox 20% of time), and able to meet the requirements for site access at CNL’s Chalk River Laboratories (i.e. security clearance).
Nice to Have
• Experience in deal structuring or commercial negotiations, strategic partnerships or alliances, or service-line or product management.
• Experience in, or advising clients in, energy, nuclear, aerospace, defence, or another regulated, highly engineered sector, including FOAK or R&D programs.
• Genuine interest in fusion, clean energy, or deep tech, and in helping an early-stage company scale.
• Medical, dental and vision benefit.
• Competitive paid vacation and sick time.
• Small, tight-knit team with low barriers to action.
• Exposure to a wide variety of problems for unparalleled, hands‑on professional growth.

Job summary
• Own day-to-day digital campaign operations (display, programmatic, social, video, search-support) in collaboration with Subject matter experts (SME’s), with additional responsibility for pixel strategy, measurement hygiene and data governance.
• Ensure campaigns launch on time, run smoothly, meet quality standards and deliver against client KPIs under guidance from senior ops/strategy leads.

Key responsibilities
• Campaign Trafficking & setup
• Configure campaigns in ad servers/DSPs/SSPs and social platforms; apply targeting, creatives, tracking pixels and third‑party tags according to specs.
• Validate creative specs, creative-size compatibility and URL redirects.
• Pixel strategy & measurement design
• Develop and maintain a pixel/event taxonomy that maps site/app events to campaign KPIs and attribution modeling needs.
• Define standard naming conventions, event parameters, value fields and deduplication rules across platforms.
• Recommend and implement client-appropriate measurement approaches: client-side pixels (Meta, Google, TikTok), server-to-server (S2S) or hybrid solutions for reliability and privacy resilience.
• Align pixel strategy with reporting needs (last-click, data-driven attribution, incrementality) and with analytics teams.
• Tag management & implementation
• Coordinate with development teams for hard-coded or SDK event implementations, and support QA of mobile SDK events.
• QA, testing & troubleshooting
• Create and run pixel QA checklists: verify event firing, parameter accuracy, dedupe, conversion priorities and proper conversions attribution.
• Use browser dev tools, tag debuggers, network inspectors and platform pixel helpers to diagnose issues; escalate to engineering when necessary.
• Monitor and resolve tag duplication, missing events, or mismatched parameter values.
• Campaign monitoring, pacing & optimization
• Monitor delivery, pacing, budgets and inventory; implement optimizations (bids, audiences, creative rotation) guided by performance leads.
• Use pixel-derived conversion data to fuel optimizations and audience building (retargeting / lookalike).
• Reporting & insights
• Produce client/internal performance reports and maintain dashboards that use validated pixel data, surface insights and optimization recommendations.
• Track data quality KPIs (pixel firing rate, event completion rate) and report issues proactively.
• Cross-functional coordination & vendor liaison
• Liaise with strategy/account, analytics, Ad Ops and Marketing Science teams to align on timelines, specs and deliverables.
• Manage routine communication with ad tech vendors, measurement partners and publishers for troubleshooting and implementation support.
• Documentation & process improvement
• Maintain pixel strategy docs, event taxonomies, implementation guides, SOPs and post-campaign retrospectives; propose process improvements and automation opportunities.

Tools & tech familiarity
• Tag managers: Google Tag Manager,
• Pixels & SDKs: Meta Pixel, Google Ads/GA4, TikTok, LinkedIn, custom S2S implementations
• Ad tech: DV360, The Trade Desk, Google Ad Manager, social ad managers
• Analytics & reporting: GA4, Google Campaign Manager

Skills & qualifications
• 2-3 years in ad ops/digital campaign operations at an agency or in-house media role, with direct pixel/tagging experience
• Strong attention to detail, analytical mindset and problem-solving skills
• Practical experience with GTM/dataLayer and event taxonomy design
• Good communicator; able to translate technical measurement issues for non-technical stakeholders

KPIs / success metrics (measurement-focused)
• Pixel/event firing accuracy (target 98%+)
• Event completeness rate (conversion events captured vs expected)
• On-time launch rate (95%+)
• Budget pacing accuracy (within agreed tolerances)
• Mean time to resolve measurement/tagging issues

Typical deliverables
• Pixel strategy & event taxonomy document mapping events to KPIs
• Pixel QA checklists and troubleshooting runbooks
• Daily/weekly performance dashboards using validated conversion data
• Post-campaign measurement audit and recommendations

Growth expectations
• Independently execute medium-complexity campaigns and own pixel implementations for small to mid-size clients.
• Advice on measurement resilience (server-side, clean rooms) and privacy-safe data strategies as part of career progression.
• Develop automation and technical reporting skills (SQL, server-side tagging) to advance to senior ops or measurement roles.

Thumbtack helps millions of people confidently care for their homes.

Thumbtack is the one app you need to take care of and improve your home — from personalized guidance to AI tools and a best-in-class hiring experience. Every day in every county of the U.S., people turn to Thumbtack to complete urgent repairs, seasonal maintenance and bigger improvements. We help homeowners know which projects to do, when to do them and who to hire from our growing community of 300,000 local service businesses. If making an impact inspires you, join us. Imagine what we’ll build together.

About The Commercial Strategy Team

The Commercial Strategy team sits within the Business Development & Commercial Programs org and is responsible for helping take ideas from 0 to 1 by leading strategic initiatives and bets, and partnering cross functionally with other teams to test, experiment, and implement new strategies. The Partner Operations sub-team is the engine behind Thumbtack's partnerships business. We build the scalable systems, processes, and infrastructure that turn partner opportunities into operational reality. Beyond running the day-to-day, we lead high-priority strategic initiatives and early-stage pilots that don't fit neatly into existing lanes, coordinate cross-functionally to align workflows and ownership for new capabilities, and drive the transition from pilot to scalable operations. When we do our job well, partners grow, capabilities expand, and revenue grows.

About The Role

As the Manager, Launch and Growth Operations, you will lead a portfolio of strategic programs that help grow and scale Thumbtack’s partnerships business. Reporting to the Senior Manager of Partnership Operations, you’ll manage a globally distributed team across the U.S. and the Philippines while working across the organization to turn high-potential opportunities into durable business capabilities.

You will operate at the intersection of strategy, program leadership, and operations. Your work may include building and scaling new growth programs, developing go-to-market strategies, improving business performance and economics, strengthening partner-facing capabilities, and evolving the systems and processes that support our partnerships. Initial priorities will include launching new partnerships, scaling Call Center, and advancing our Partner Operations foundation, but your portfolio will evolve alongside the needs of the business.

This is a high-impact player-coach role for a versatile operator who can set direction, lead complex execution, and deliver measurable outcomes. You will bring structure to ambiguous opportunities, move fluidly between strategy and execution, and align teams across functions to take programs from concept through launch and scale.

What You’ll Do

• Lead a portfolio of strategic programs: Lead and own high-impact initiatives that accelerate the growth and scalability of Thumbtack’s partnerships business
• Build and scale new business capabilities: Take emerging opportunities from concept through launch and scale, establishing the operating processes, systems, and cross-functional model required for reliable execution.
• Own measurable business outcomes: Define success measures, monitor performance, identify limiting factors, and make clear recommendations that improve growth, efficiency, operational performance, and program economics.
• Lead complex programs end to end: Serve as the central hub across Product, Engineering, Data Science, Marketing, Commercial Operations, Commercial Strategy, Legal, and external partners to translate strategy into coordinated execution
• Shape strategy through analytical insight: Use data, customer and partner insights, and structured problem-solving to evaluate opportunities, make tradeoffs, and influence investment decisions
• Strengthen the Partner Operations foundation: Improve the tools, systems, processes, and operating models that enable partnerships to launch and scale reliably
• Lead a globally distributed team: Set a clear vision and priorities while managing and developing a team across the U.S. and the Philippines to become increasingly independent owners

In order to be successful, you must bring

• 5+ years of experience in strategy and operations, business operations, program management, general management, management consulting, or a related field
• 2+ years of people-management experience, with a demonstrated ability to set direction, develop talent, and lead a team of operators
• Experience translating ambiguous business opportunities into clear strategies, operating plans, and measurable results
• A track record of leading complex initiatives from concept through execution, including stepping toward problems and taking accountability when results fall short
• Strong business judgment and analytical rigor, with the ability to assess performance, understand economics, evaluate tradeoffs, and determine where to invest
• Clear, influential communication skills, with the ability to create a compelling vision, distill complexity, align diverse stakeholders, and influence without authority
• An owner mentality, strong learning agility, a bias for action, and a low-ego approach to leadership and collaboration

Expected salary ranges

• For candidates living in Ontario and British Columbia, the expected total cash compensation (base salary + variable pay, if applicable) range for this role is currently $126,700.00 - $163,900.00.

Actual offered salaries will vary and will be based on various factors, such as calibrated job level, qualifications, skills, competencies, and proficiency for the role.
